answer_text:
We are given

\[
f(x)=\int_0^x (x-t^2)g(t)\,dt.
\]

Differentiate using the Leibniz integral rule. Since the integrand depends on \(x\),

\[
f'(x)=(x-x^2)g(x)+\int_0^x g(t)\,dt.
\]

Now differentiate again:

\[
f''(x)=(1-2x)g(x)+(x-x^2)g'(x)+g(x).
\]

Simplify:

\[
f''(x)=2(1-x)g(x)+x(1-x)g'(x)
\]

\[
f''(x)=(1-x)\bigl(2g(x)+xg'(x)\bigr).
\]

Therefore,

\[
f''(1)=(1-1)\bigl(2g(1)+1\cdot g'(1)\bigr)=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
